original_value: We present a first prototype of a wideband microwave tomography system with potential application to medical imaging. The system relies on a compact and robust printed monopole antenna which can operate in the 1.0–3.0 GHz range when fully immersed in commonly used coupling liquids, such as glycerine–water solutions. By simulating the proposed imaging setup in CST Microwave Studio, we study the signal transmission levels and array sensitivity for different target and coupling liquid media. We then present the experimental prototype design and data acquisition process, and show good agreement between experimentally measured data and results from the CST simulations. We assess imaging performance by applying our previously proposed two-dimensional (2-D) DBIM TwIST-algorithm to both simulated and experimental datasets, and demonstrate that the system can reconstruct simple cylindrical targets at multiple frequencies.

result.paraphrase: We introduce an initial wideband microwave tomography prototype intended for medical imaging. It uses a compact, robust printed monopole antenna that operates from 1.0 to 3.0 GHz when fully immersed in commonly used coupling liquids, including glycerine–water solutions. Using CST Microwave Studio to simulate the proposed imaging arrangement, we examine signal transmission levels and array sensitivity across different target and coupling-liquid media. We also describe the experimental prototype and data acquisition procedure, and find good agreement between measured results and CST simulations. To evaluate imaging performance, we apply our previously proposed two-dimensional (2-D) DBIM TwIST algorithm to both simulated and experimental datasets, showing that the system can reconstruct simple cylindrical targets at multiple frequencies.
